# Tavily (4 endpoints)

## Endpoints

| Resource | Params | Credits | Description |
|----------|--------|---------|-------------|
| /search | `query` | 1 | Tavily web search with optional LLM-generated answer |
| /extract | `urls` | 1 | Extract clean content from one or more URLs |
| /map | `url` | 1 | Map a website's sitegraph |
| /crawl | `url` | 1 | Crawl a website with LLM-driven path selection |

### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /search — 1cr

Runs a web search via Tavily and returns ranked results plus an optional LLM-generated `answer` synthesised from the top sources. Set `include_answer=true` to enable answer synthesis. Use `search_depth=advanced` for higher-relevance results (also unlocks `chunks_per_source`). Filter results to specific domains via `include_domains` (comma-separated), or exclude via `exclude_domains`. Time-bounded queries via `time_range` (`d` / `w` / `m` / `y`) or explicit `start_date` / `end_date` (YYYY-MM-DD).

**Parameters**

- `query`: The search query — natural-language free text.
- `search_depth` *(optional)*: Latency-vs-relevance tradeoff. `basic` is the default; `advanced` unlocks `chunks_per_source` and higher-relevance ranking.
- `topic` *(optional)*: Search category. Defaults to `general`. Use `news` for time-sensitive queries and `finance` for market data.
- `time_range` *(optional)*: Time window relative to now. Accepts `day` / `week` / `month` / `year` (or shorthand `d` / `w` / `m` / `y`).
- `max_results` *(optional)*: Number of results to return (1–20). Defaults to 5.
- `chunks_per_source` *(optional)*: Max relevant chunks returned per source (1–5). Only honoured when `search_depth=advanced`. Defaults to 3.
- `include_images` *(optional)*: Include images alongside the result content.
- `include_image_descriptions` *(optional)*: Include AI-generated descriptions for the returned images.
- `include_answer` *(optional)*: Include an LLM-generated answer string synthesised from the top sources.
- `include_raw_content` *(optional)*: Include the raw HTML/text alongside the cleaned content.
- `include_domains` *(optional)*: Comma-separated list of domains to restrict results to (e.g. `nytimes.com,reuters.com`).
- `exclude_domains` *(optional)*: Comma-separated list of domains to exclude from results.
- `country` *(optional)*: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code to bias results toward.
- `start_date` *(optional)*: Inclusive lower bound on result publish date (YYYY-MM-DD).
- `end_date` *(optional)*: Inclusive upper bound on result publish date (YYYY-MM-DD).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tavily/search?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /extract — 1cr

Pulls clean, AI-ready text out of one or more URLs via Tavily's extractor. Pass a single URL or a comma-separated list (max 20). Returns extracted content per URL alongside any URLs that failed extraction. Use `extract_depth=advanced` for harder pages (paywalls, JS-heavy SPAs).

**Parameters**

- `urls`: Comma-separated list of URLs to extract (max 20).
- `extract_depth` *(optional)*: Extraction strategy. `basic` is the default and faster; `advanced` handles harder pages but takes longer.
- `format` *(optional)*: Output format for the extracted content. `markdown` (default) preserves structure; `text` is plain.
- `include_images` *(optional)*: Include images extracted from each URL.
- `include_favicon` *(optional)*: Include the favicon URL for each page.
- `timeout` *(optional)*: Per-URL timeout in seconds (1–60).

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tavily/extract?urls=<urls>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /map — 1cr

Returns the sitegraph of a website starting from a root URL — a list of discovered URLs without their full content. Cheaper and faster than crawl when you only need to enumerate pages (e.g. for sitemap discovery or coverage analysis). Use `instructions` to guide the mapper in natural language and the `select_*` / `exclude_*` filters (regex patterns, comma-separated) to narrow scope.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Root URL to begin mapping.
- `max_depth` *(optional)*: Maximum link depth from the root URL. Defaults to 1.
- `max_breadth` *(optional)*: Maximum number of links followed per level (per page). Defaults to 20.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Total number of links the mapper will process before stopping. Defaults to 50.
- `instructions` *(optional)*: Natural-language instructions for the mapper (e.g. 'Find all pages related to API documentation').
- `select_paths` *(optional)*: Comma-separated regex patterns — only include URLs whose path matches.
- `select_domains` *(optional)*: Comma-separated regex patterns — only include URLs whose domain matches.
- `exclude_paths` *(optional)*: Comma-separated regex patterns — exclude URLs whose path matches.
- `exclude_domains` *(optional)*: Comma-separated regex patterns — exclude URLs whose domain matches.
- `allow_external` *(optional)*: Whether to follow / return links to external domains. Defaults to true.
- `timeout` *(optional)*: Maximum time in seconds (10–150).
- `categories` *(optional)*: Comma-separated list of category hints to bias mapping toward.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tavily/map?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /crawl — 1cr

Multi-page crawl starting from a root URL. Returns each crawled page with its extracted content (unlike map, which returns only URLs). Use `instructions` to guide the crawler in natural language — Tavily uses an LLM to follow only the paths matching your intent. Use `select_*` / `exclude_*` filters (comma-separated regex patterns) to constrain scope.

**Parameters**

- `url`: Root URL to begin crawling.
- `max_depth` *(optional)*: Maximum link depth from the root URL. Defaults to 1.
- `max_breadth` *(optional)*: Maximum number of links followed per level (per page). Defaults to 20.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Total number of pages the crawler will process before stopping. Defaults to 50.
- `instructions` *(optional)*: Natural-language instructions for the crawler (e.g. 'Find all product pages with pricing').
- `select_paths` *(optional)*: Comma-separated regex patterns — only crawl URLs whose path matches.
- `select_domains` *(optional)*: Comma-separated regex patterns — only crawl URLs whose domain matches.
- `exclude_paths` *(optional)*: Comma-separated regex patterns — skip URLs whose path matches.
- `exclude_domains` *(optional)*: Comma-separated regex patterns — skip URLs whose domain matches.
- `allow_external` *(optional)*: Whether to follow links to external domains. Defaults to true.
- `extract_depth` *(optional)*: Per-page extraction strategy. `basic` is faster; `advanced` handles harder pages.
- `format` *(optional)*: Output format for extracted content. `markdown` (default) or `text`.
- `categories` *(optional)*: Comma-separated list of category hints to bias the crawl toward.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/tavily/crawl?url=<url>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## Choosing a Tavily endpoint

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| Web search, optionally with an LLM answer | `/search` | 1 |
| Clean text out of URLs you already have | `/extract` | 1 |
| What pages exist on this site | `/map` | 1 |
| Crawl a site, LLM choosing the paths | `/crawl` | 1 |

All 1 credit — which makes Tavily the cheapest general web toolkit in the API.

### Tavily or `web`?

They overlap. The deciding factor is cost shape: `web/scrape` is 1cr, `web/search` is 2cr and
`web/extract` is 5cr, while every Tavily endpoint is 1cr. For search and structured extraction,
**Tavily is cheaper**. Reach for `web` when you need what Tavily has no equivalent for: async
crawl jobs, page monitors, interactive sessions, or document parsing.

`/search` with the LLM answer enabled is a one-call research primitive — the answer plus its
citations, for a single credit. `perplexity/research` (1cr) does the same job with a different
model behind it; `prism/answers` (15cr) runs Perplexity, Grok and Tavily together and returns
an agreement matrix when the question is contested enough to want consensus.

## Optional params


### `search`

| `search_depth` | `basic` (default) / `advanced` / `fast` / `ultra-fast` |
| `topic` | `general` (default) / `news` / `finance` |

| `max_results` | 1–20, default 5 |

| `include_raw_content` | Boolean |
| `include_domains` / `exclude_domains` | CSV — domain filters |
| `country` | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code |
| `start_date` / `end_date` | YYYY-MM-DD bounds |

### `extract`

| Param | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `extract_depth` | `basic` (default) / `advanced` |
| `format` | `markdown` (default) / `text` |
| `include_images` / `include_favicon` | Booleans |
| `timeout` | Per-URL timeout, 1–60s |

### `map` / `crawl`

| Param | Notes |
|-------|-------|
| `max_depth` | Default 1 |
| `max_breadth` | Default 20 (per-page link cap) |
| `limit` | Default 50 (total pages) |
| `instructions` | Natural-language guidance for the mapper / crawler |
| `select_paths` / `select_domains` | CSV regex whitelist |
| `exclude_paths` / `exclude_domains` | CSV regex blacklist |
| `allow_external` | Boolean, default `true` |
| `categories` | CSV category hints |
| `extract_depth` / `format` | `crawl` only — same as `extract` |

## Field Maps


None. All four endpoints are passthrough. Archetype: `Analytics` — preserves the full Tavily response (`results`, `answer`, `query_analysis`, `suggestions`, `total_results`, `time_taken`). Using `SearchResult` would silently drop the LLM-generated `answer` field, which is the whole point of Tavily.

Empty `results: []` is billed normally as a successful 200 — the user paid for the search, an empty result is a real answer.
